title: The IF function: choosing with a condition
summary: IF tests a condition and returns one value if it is true and another if it is false.
intro: `IF` lets a formula make a decision: if the condition is met it returns the first value, otherwise the second. Both values can be text between quotation marks, numbers or other formulas.
args: What to return if the condition is met.
What to return if it is not. If you leave it out, IF returns `FALSE`.
examples: Row 2 sales are 120, so the condition is true.
Row 3 sales are 80, so the condition is false.
errors: Text typed without quotation marks, such as `=IF(C2>100,High,Normal)`.

faq.q: How do I test more than one condition?
faq.a: Put `AND` or `OR` where the condition goes, such as `=IF(AND(C2>50,B2="North"),"Yes","No")`.

faq.q: Can IF return an empty cell?
faq.a: Yes, use `""` as the value, such as `=IF(C2>100,"High","")`.
